subject: Post-demo: model evals & multilingual checks (EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicretail.se>, Kenji Tanaka <kenji.tanaka@kizuna.co.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T14:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: model evals & multilingual checks (EU/APAC)

Hi Anna / Kenji —

Thanks again for the demo time today — great convo and helpful context on the checklist and internationalization constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- What we heard: primary languages of interest are Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish for EU; Japanese, Korean, Thai for APAC. Main quality concerns are proper handling of locale-specific terminology (product names, local place names), date/number formats, and customer-name transliteration.

- Immediate deliverables from Redwood (proposed timeline):
  1) Per-locale automated evals + short human review for a 200-sample seed set (5 business days) — we’ll share results and clear pass/fail thresholds.
  2) Recommended model variants and quantization profiles per workload (2 business days).
  3) Prompt-set examples and a small “instruction + slot” template for each language (attached).
  4) Cost/throughput estimate for both Hosted API and Dedicated capacity options (Neha will follow up).

- Initial model recommendations (subject to evals):
  - EU lightweight: Redwood-13B-compact (quantized q4f) — good latency/cost for chat-like tasks.
  - EU high-quality: Redwood-70B-llm (mixed-precision) — best for nuanced translation/locale fidelity if you need the highest quality.
  - APAC: Redwood-13B + language-specific adapter/finetune for Japanese/Korean; test both base and adapter variants.

I’ve attached a seed prompt-set (prompt-sets-nordic-apac.csv) and an initial PDF with our automated eval summary (nr_multilingual_eval_results_v1.pdf). Also linking our eval dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/NR-2026-044.

Next step: I’ll run the per-locale automated evals first thing tomorrow and share the results. If you’d like, we can book a 30-minute sync next week to review the results and an ops-runbook for rollout.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: prompt-sets-nordic-apac.csv, nr_multilingual_eval_results_v1.pdf
From: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicretail.se>

Date: 2026-06-22T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model evals & multilingual checks (EU/APAC)

Hi Marissa —

Really helpful recap, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Language priority for us is Swedish and Finnish first, Danish/Norwegian second. For APAC, prioritize Japanese, then Korean. Thai is lower priority but still important for the roadmap.
- Critical quality requirements: correct inflection for product descriptions, proper handling of EU-specific legal terms (we have a short glossary we can share), and handling of multi-word customer names (no forced transliteration).
- Can you confirm what the automated evals will measure? For us we need both token-level metrics and a small human review for cultural/NUANCE failures.

Also, curious about latency/throughput when using the Dedicated option from a EU region — we have spikes during promotions and need to understand scaling behavior.

If you can include a short example prompt per language and the evaluation thresholds you recommend, that would be super useful.

Best,
Anna Svensson
Localization Lead, NordicRetail AB
anna.svensson@nordicretail.se
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicretail.se>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T08:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model evals & multilingual checks (EU/APAC)

Hi Anna —

Thanks — noted the priority order. To answer your questions and be explicit on scope: 

Automated eval plan (what we’ll run):
- Metrics: token-level perplexity (relative), chrF for surface-level string similarity, and intent-preservation score from a lightweight classifier.
- Human review: 200 samples (per locale) with 3 human annotators for edge-case categories (legal terms, names, cultural tone). We’ll surface examples and a short set of failure categories.

Recommended thresholds (initial):
- chrF >= 0.55 for templated responses, >=0.45 for open generation.
- Intent preservation >= 90% on classifier holdout.
- Failure rate on human review: target <= 5% for high-priority locales.

Model guidance (more detail):
- Swedish/Scandi (cost-sensitive): Redwood-13B-compact (q4f) — target lowest latency with acceptable chrF.
- Swedish/Scandi (quality-sensitive): Redwood-70B-llm — we expect improvement on subtle morphology and legal phrasing.
- Japanese/Korean: Redwood-13B + language adapters — adapters reduce cost and often close the gap vs. full 70B for specific languages. We’ll test both adapter and small finetune on a 5k-sample dev set.

Attachments: prompt-sets-nordic-apac.csv (examples per locale). I’ve queued the per-locale automated runs; results will be in your drive link and on the eval dashboard by EOD tomorrow. 

Jonas — can you spin up the EU dedicated benchmark (eu-west-1) and run the 1k-token/throughput profile Anna mentioned? Please include tail-latency (p95/p99) and autoscaling behavior.

Neha — can you draft a 90-day reserved capacity quote for both committed and burst options once Jonas posts the numbers?

Thanks —
Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T15:25:00Z
Subject: Action items: NR-2026-044 — benchmarks & pricing

Jonas / Neha — quick action list following Anna’s ask and the queued evals: 

- Jonas: please run the Dedicated EU benchmark in eu-west-1 with the following profiles:
  * Baseline chat (256 token context) — 100 rps sustained, record p95/p99 latencies.
  * Promo spike (1 minute bursts at 600 rps) — measure autoscale time to steady-state and fallback behavior.
  * Memory/kv-cache hit-rate report for the adapter workflow.
  Deliverable: spreadsheet with throughput/latency numbers + short notes on recommended autoscale policy. Attach to the drive folder.

- Neha: prepare 90-day and 12-month reserved capacity pricing, include cost delta for adapter vs full-model hosting, and suggested SLA tiers (99.9% / 99.95%).

I’ll consolidate the per-locale human-review plan once the automated evals land. Expected internal ETA: Jonas results by EOD tomorrow, Neha quote in 2 business days.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
